causebase_summary: According to its website, the Aboriginal Legal Rights Movement (ALRM) is an Aboriginal community-controlled legal service based in South Australia, with a main office in Adelaide on Kaurna land. causebase_summary: According to the organisation's website and its ACNC reporting, Banks Street Newmarket Community Preschooling Centre Inc (Banks Street Kindy) is a small not‑for‑profit community kindergarten located on the grounds of Newmarket State School in Newmarket, Queensland. The website describes educator‑led early childhood learning with daily outdoor play across multiple outdoor areas (sandpit, mud kitchen, fairy garden), regular visits to the neighbouring Banks Street Reserve (described as a “Bush Kindy” day), and on‑site chickens named Rainbow and Lamington. The site names a Kindy Director, Sharon Kemp, and an art teacher, Kath, and says the kindergarten holds an annual art show for families. The website describes a volunteer kindy management committee, fundraising activity, and connections with Newmarket State School (library visits and participation in school events). The site also describes a daily acknowledgement of Country, a Welcome to Country song, and visits from Aunty Sharron and Uncle Bruce to teach about First Nations culture. The ACNC AIS 2023 extract in the supplied evidence lists revenue of AUD 437,441 and total expenses of AUD 385,269 for the 2023 year.

causebase_summary: The organisation’s website describes Accelerated Evolution - The Break Inc. as a volunteer-run, not-for-profit mental health and wellbeing recovery provider based in Victoria. causebase_summary: Global Wildlife Fund Limited is described on its website as an Australian charity, based in New South Wales, that partners with local conservation organisations to fund and oversee overseas conservation projects. The organisation lists initial geographic priorities as Sub‑Saharan Africa, the Andes–Amazon, New Guinea and the Pacific, and Asian biodiversity hotspots. Website material and news items cited include wildlife translocations (for example, reintroduction of black rhino to Matusadona National Park and translocation of sable antelope in Zimbabwe), a Papua Community Forest Project that aims to help communities secure customary title and implement forest management to prevent industrial logging, and purchase of 250 hectares to expand Narupa Reserve in the Ecuadorian Amazon. The site names target species and groups such as black rhino, snow leopards, African wild dogs, hummingbirds, macaws, birds of paradise and rediscovered marsupials in Papua. The organisation states it negotiates project funding agreements, tracks project progress and reports back on outcomes and metrics. The website also states that directors and founders donate their time to research, assess, support and audit projects and that Australians can make tax‑deductible gifts.

causebase_summary: The APNIC Foundation Limited is a Queensland-registered organisation that the Foundation’s 2025 annual report describes as an Asia Pacific digital development organisation. (a cohort of 150 women and gender-diverse participants across six Southeast Asian economies), Digital Leap South Asia (DLSA in three South Asian economies) and the RISE‑PH ISIF grantee that the report says connected 53 school sites (51 public schools and 2 teacher‑training colleges; an estimated 80,000–100,000 students). causebase_summary: Fight Cancer Foundation (formerly Bone Marrow Donor Institute) is described on its website as a national charity. The organisation’s 2015 annual report outlines multiple service streams. An education support program called Back on Track places specialist Education Advisors (trained teachers) in children’s hospitals to provide one-to-one tutoring, group learning sessions, Individual Learning Plans, liaison with schools and clinical teams, and transition planning for learners receiving cancer treatment; the report gives a detailed daily schedule of advisor activities. The report also describes three accommodation centres—Hilltop (Albury), John Opie House (Hobart) and BMDI Rotary House (North Melbourne)—that provide short-term, subsidised accommodation to patients and families who must travel for treatment; house managers handle bookings, patient travel assistance invoicing, waiting lists and on-site issues. The report states involvement with the BMDI Cord Blood Bank in Melbourne (reporting more than 12,700 cord blood units stored and 525 releases for transplant) and ongoing links with the Australian Bone Marrow Donor Registry via a board position. The organisation’s materials note volunteer directors, volunteers and patrons, and describe events, fundraising and research scholarships in support of these programs.

causebase_summary: The Healing Foundation (registered in the ACT per ACNC records) describes itself as a national Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander organisation that works with Stolen Generations survivors, their families and communities. The site lists more than 50 downloadable resources (fact sheets, reports, toolkits and videos), runs online events and public forums, and in 2026 announced a $200,000 grants program for Stolen Generations truth‑telling projects. causebase_summary: The organisation’s website describes Dieback Working Group Inc as a WA‑based group focused on Phytophthora cinnamomi (Phytophthora Dieback). causebase_summary: Angel Gowns Australia Incorporated is a volunteer-run charity that repurposes donated wedding and evening-wear fabrics into garments and related items for bereaved families, hospitals and funeral homes. The organisation’s 2021 annual report states it had over 370 volunteers across all states and territories, organised seamstress, tutu-maker and de-constructor roles, and named a management committee and state coordinators. Program activity described in that report includes: handcrafting Angel Gown garments and micro-gowns; producing more than 60 tutus in the past 12 months using salvaged tulle (stock gifted to Ronald McDonald House Perth, Perth Children’s Hospital, Royal Children’s Hospital Melbourne and Women’s and Children’s Hospital Adelaide); creating an Early Loss Pouch for babies under 20 weeks; and fulfilling special requests (report lists specific gifts such as eight poem cards with crystals, multiple micro-gown/wrap packs and larger gowns). The report records the service being stocked by 211 hospitals and 102 funeral homes and notes logistics challenges during COVID (storage access, delivery delays with TOLL/AusPost). The organisation’s 2022–23 regulatory reporting shows revenue of AUD 14,107 and expenses of AUD 23,383.

causebase_summary: Australian Design Centre (ADC) is presented on its website as a Sydney-based organisation that curates and tours design exhibitions, operates a retail Object Shop and publishes research into design. The site describes “ADC On Tour,” saying that “since the 1970s ADC has toured nationally” to provide regional Australia with access to exhibitions. The Object Shop is described as supporting “over 150 leading and emerging Australian designer makers.” The website lists government partners including NSW Government, City of Sydney and Australian Government (Visions of Australia). The ACNC AIS 2023 extract in the evidence pack reports revenue of AUD 1,403,560 and total expenses of AUD 1,364,655 for 2023. The website also contains an Announcement Board item about a Board decision on ADC’s future and a December 2025 feedback survey about the impact of “ADC closing.”

causebase_summary: Adelaide City Mosque (listed on the ACNC as ADELAIDE MOSQUE ISLAMIC SOCIETY LTD and also referred to on its website as Adelaide Mosque Islamic Society of SA Inc) is a mosque in Adelaide, South Australia. The website describes the building as the oldest functioning mosque in Australia, built in 1886–88 by migrant cameleers from Afghanistan, north‑west India (now Pakistan) and Balochistan. The organisation publishes daily prayer times and a Friday Juma time and says it offers five daily prayers and other facilities. Named services and activities on the website include Prayers/Salah services, funeral services, and halal certification. It lists religious programs and events such as Ramadan, Mawlid‑un‑Nabi and Shab e Miraj, and community activities including a children’s school and a “Sister’s Morning Tea.” The site invites community membership, accepts donations (PayPal, debit/credit card and direct deposit) for general mosque support and specific purposes (iftar, zakat, sadqa, mawlid), and notes website support from the Department of Premier and Cabinet – Multicultural Affairs. The ACNC entry for the legal entity was observed; detailed financial statements and published information on program scale are not included in the supplied evidence.

causebase_summary: Rossmoyne Kindergarten Association (Inc.) operates Rossmoyne Community Kindergarten, described on its website as a community-run kindergarten leased from the City of Canning and operating since 1969. The website states the kindergarten has two classes with a maximum of 20 children each (a stated staff-to-children ratio of 2:20) and that teachers are appointed by the Department of Education while the service is managed by a parent committee. The site describes an on-site “Enchanted Garden” nature play area with a water pump, sandpits, forts, chickens, rabbits, guinea pigs and vegetable patches and says these features support children’s cognitive and emotional development. Enrolment is described as an in-person, two-step process through Rossmoyne Primary School with an intake preference for local-area residents and siblings; the site states a maximum of 40 kindergarten places per year. The website lists the current cost as A$820 per year (A$205 per term), notes the service relies on community support including grants, donations and volunteers, and offers both an on-site tour and a 360-degree virtual tour. ACNC extracts and the AIS 2023 are listed as regulatory sources; AIS 2023 reports revenue of A$48,227 and expenses of A$49,568.

causebase_summary: The Australian Community Transport Association (ACTA) presents itself as a national membership body for community transport providers, stating membership from “100+” organisations across all states and territories. ACTA’s website describes its stated activities as policy reform, sector leadership, advocacy for transport equity and support for service providers; it publishes news about webinars, a national conference and a National Community Transport Pricing Model (NCTPM) pilot run with iMove and the University of South Australia. The site reports aggregate figures attributed to its membership: 6.05 million trips per year, 261,800 clients served and 104.5 million kilometres of travel. ACTA’s online description characterises “community transport” services (as delivered by members) as person‑centred transport for older Australians, people with disability, carers and others facing transport disadvantage across metropolitan, regional, rural and remote communities.
